NSE & BSE PRE-OPEN SESSION RULES & EQUILIBRIUM PRICE DISCOVERY

1. Why Was Pre-Open Introduced by Stock Exchanges?

Prior to 2010, the market opened continuously at 09:15 AM, resulting in extreme opening volatility and manipulation. Pre-Open (09:00 - 09:15 AM) was introduced by SEBI, NSE, and BSE to conduct an order accumulation and multilateral equilibrium price discovery auction, ensuring fair, non-volatile opening prices for all equities and indices.

2. The 3 Official Exchange Session Phases
  • Phase 1: 09:00 AM - 09:08 AM (Order Collection Period): Investors place, modify, or cancel Limit and Market orders. No trade execution occurs during this period.
  • Phase 2: 09:08 AM - 09:12 AM (Order Matching & IEP Discovery): The exchange system freezes order modifications and executes multilateral matching algorithm to discover the Indicative Equilibrium Price (IEP).
  • Phase 3: 09:12 AM - 09:15 AM (Buffer Period): System transition buffer to ensure a smooth rollover into continuous trading at 09:15 AM. Unmatched orders are automatically transferred to the regular order book.
3. How Is the Indicative Equilibrium Price (IEP) Calculated?

The exchange matching algorithm selects the single equilibrium opening price based on 3 hierarchical criteria:

  1. Maximum Tradable Volume: The price at which the highest quantity of buy and sell orders can be matched.
  2. Minimum Order Imbalance: If multiple prices have the same maximum tradable volume, the price with the lowest surplus (unmatched) orders is chosen.
  3. Closer to Previous Close: If a tie still remains, the price nearest to the previous trading day's closing price is selected as the official Opening Price.
4. Pro Pre-Open Trading Strategies (Gap & Go vs Gap Fade)
  • Gap & Go (Momentum Breakout): When IEP opens > +1.5% above Previous Day High with Buy Demand > 2x Sell Supply and unmatched buy surplus. Enter on 09:15 opening candle breakout.
  • Gap Fade / S&R Trap: When IEP opens directly into a major Resistance Wall (R2/R3) with heavy Call Writing, look for the opening trap reversal targeting Central Pivot.

METHOD 1: BREAKOUT & RETEST TRENDING

When price breaks through Resistance, do NOT enter right away. Wait for the retest! Former resistance becomes new support. Look for a bullish rejection candle (pin-bar/hammer) bouncing off the retest — that is your confirmed entry.

• Entry: Retest rejection candle close
• Stop Loss: Just below retested support
METHOD 2: KEY LEVEL REVERSAL RANGE BOUND

When market rallies to Resistance and gets strongly rejected with long upper wicks, wait for the next candle to close firmly below it. Enter short with high conviction as liquidity dries up.

• Entry: Reversal candle close below resistance
• Stop Loss: Just above key resistance
METHOD 3: TRAP TRADING (#1 ACCURACY) 👑 CROWN JEWEL

Retail breakout buyers jump in on first resistance break. The market traps them with a big red candle hitting retail stop-losses. Then true institutional smart money reclaims with explosive momentum on the second breakout!

• Entry: Confirmed 2nd breakout / reclaim
• Stop Loss: Just below support / trap wick

MASTERCLASS 201 QUANTITATIVE ALGORITHMS • ORDER FLOW MATHEMATICS

Advanced AI Indicators & Mathematical Formulations

Step-by-step breakdown of the exact algorithmic formulas used by the Claude AI Day Trader Skill, including Relative Volume (RVOL), HyperFlow™ momentum vector scoring, Order Flow Delta, Central Pivot Range, and Put-Call Ratio dynamics.

Engine: Claude 3.5 Sonnet Quant
Sampling Rate: Tick-by-Tick Depth
Indicators: 5 Core Quant Pillars

1. Relative Volume (RVOL) — The Institutional Fingerprint

Formula Math

Raw volume numbers can be misleading. Relative Volume calculates current cumulative volume relative to the exact minute's 20-day historical average:

RVOL(t) = Cumulative Volume(t) / Average Cumulative Volume(t, 20 Days)
RVOL < 1.0x Low volume retail chop. Breakouts frequently fail. Do NOT trade.
RVOL 1.5x – 2.0x Active institutional interest. High-probability continuation setups.
RVOL ≥ 2.5x Institutional Whale Flow. Major sustained trend day with low slippage.

2. HyperFlow™ Momentum Matrix (Score 0 to 100)

AI Scoring

HyperFlow™ combines Order Flow Delta velocity, distance from Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP), and rate of Open Interest accumulation:

HyperFlow = 0.40 * Norm(Delta) + 0.35 * Norm(VWAP_Distance) + 0.25 * Norm(OI_Acceleration)

When HyperFlow ≥ 75, institutional buyers are aggressively paying up at the ask price. When HyperFlow ≤ 25, institutional aggressive market sells dominate.

3. Order Flow Delta & Total Bid / Ask Depth Ratio

Market Microstructure

Delta represents the net difference between aggressive buyers lifting the offer and aggressive sellers hitting the bid:

Delta = Total Executed Volume at Ask − Total Executed Volume at Bid
Bid/Ask Ratio = Total Cumulative Bid Quantity (Level-2) / Total Cumulative Ask Quantity (Level-2)

A Bid/Ask Ratio ≥ 1.25x indicates massive demand absorption (buyers stacking bids). A ratio ≤ 0.80x reveals an overhead supply wall preventing upward movement.

4. Central Pivot Range (CPR) Mechanics

Support & Resistance
Pivot (P) = (Previous High + Low + Close) / 3
Bottom Central (BC) = (Previous High + Low) / 2
Top Central (TC) = (Pivot − BC) + Pivot = 2 * Pivot − BC
Narrow CPR (Width ≤ 0.25%)

Represents market energy compression. 78% probability of an explosive Trending Day.

Wide CPR (Width ≥ 0.60%)

Represents a wide support/resistance cushion. High probability of a Rangebound / Mean-Reverting Day.

Stock Selection Strategy & Put/Call Writing Logic

Learn the step-by-step institutional filtering process to screen 218 NSE contracts down to the top 2-3 highest-probability setups each morning, verify derivative cycles, and leverage option writing support.

Filter Funnel: 218 → 12 → 3 Focus
Cycle: Long / Short Buildup
Min R:R: 1:2.0 Minimum

The 3-Step Top-Down Filtering Funnel

STEP 1: Sector Rotation

Navigate to Sector Rotation & Rank. Pick stocks belonging only to the Top 3 Sectors leading the day's turnover and % gain.

STEP 2: Quantitative Engine Check

Ensure the stock appears simultaneously in Muhurat Strong (ORB) and Muhurat Pulse (RVOL ≥ 1.8x).

STEP 3: Derivatives Buildup

Confirm the stock displays Long Buildup (Price ↑ + OI ↑) for buys or Short Buildup for sells.

The 4 Derivative Buildup Cycles Explained

CYCLE NAME PRICE OPEN INTEREST INSTITUTIONAL ACTION ACTIONABLE STRATEGY
🟢 Long Buildup RISING (↑) RISING (↑) Aggressive institutional buying with multi-day commitment. BUY Call / Long Equity
🔴 Short Buildup FALLING (↓) RISING (↑) Aggressive short sellers entering fresh bear positions. BUY Put / Short Equity
⚡ Short Covering RISING (↑) FALLING (↓) Trapped sellers panicking and buying back shares. Quick Momentum Scalp
⚠️ Long Unwind FALLING (↓) FALLING (↓) Bulls booking profits or abandoning stagnant trades. Exit Longs / Avoid Fresh Entry

Put Writing (Support) vs. Call Writing (Resistance) Logic

Institutional traders primarily write (sell) options rather than buy them. Look at the Put Writing and Call Writing columns in the screener:

🛡️ Put Writing (Support Floor)

When a stock exhibits heavy put writing at a strike below current price, institutions are betting price will NOT fall below that strike. Place your Stop-Loss just beneath this strike.

🧱 Call Writing (Resistance Ceiling)

Heavy call writing at a strike above current price acts as an institutional ceiling. Set your Target 1 just below this strike to book gains before sellers stall the move.

NIFTY 50 CPR & Options Flow Strategy Playbook

Step-by-step masterclass on trading NIFTY 50 options utilizing Central Pivot Range (CPR) boundaries, Virgin CPR magnets, Call/Put Open Interest walls, and Thursday Expiry Day Max Pain pinning.

Index: NIFTY 50 (NSE)
Lot Size: 25 / 75 Units
CPR Accuracy: > 82% Historical

The 3 High-Probability Nifty CPR Setups

SETUP A: Bullish CPR Retest (Ascending CPR Day) Win Rate: ~78%

Conditions: Today's CPR is higher than yesterday's. NIFTY opens above Top Central (TC: 24,958), pulls back between 9:45 – 10:15 AM to touch TC, and prints a bullish rejection candle (hammer or green engulfing).
Execution: BUY At-the-Money Call (e.g. 25,000 CE). Stop Loss placed 15 pts below BC (24,800). Target 1: R1 (25,124); Target 2: R2 (25,290).

SETUP B: Bearish CPR Rejection (Descending CPR Day) Win Rate: ~76%

Conditions: Today's CPR is lower than yesterday's. NIFTY opens below Bottom Central (BC: 24,815), bounces upward on low volume into Pivot or BC, and prints a red rejection candle.
Execution: BUY At-the-Money Put (e.g. 24,900 PE). Stop Loss placed 15 pts above TC (24,975). Target 1: S1 (24,720); Target 2: S2 (24,550).

SETUP C: Virgin CPR Magnetic Retest Win Rate: ~84%

Conditions: If yesterday was an extreme trend day and price never touched the CPR, it becomes a Virgin CPR. In 84% of cases, the market experiences a violent magnetic snapback to test that untouched level within 3 days.

Expiry Day Max Pain Pinning Playbook

On Thursday weekly expiry days, institutional market makers maximize premium collection by driving the index toward the Max Pain Strike (e.g. 24,950):

Morning Session (9:15 AM – 1:00 PM)

Option sellers accumulate both sides of the straddle. IV decays rapidly. Avoid buying out-of-the-money options as theta decay is brutal.

Afternoon Pinning (1:30 PM – 3:15 PM)

If Spot is within 50 pts of Max Pain, it will pin tightly. If Spot breaks past the Call Wall (25,200), initiate a Zero-Hero ATM Call trade for a 200% gamma blast.
